title: Agent Pulse
description: One daily evidence-backed decision brief from the coding-agent projects monitored by The Git Reporter.

scope.coverageStatement: V0.2 reports one dated decision brief from direct public source evidence and keeps git motion as a secondary measurement layer. Community feedback metrics are absent until a reproducible feedback collector ships.

inputs.dailyInsight: reported, date-owned Agent Pulse decision brief

editorialRead.headline: Morning Read — September 28, 2026
editorialRead.readHeadline: openclaw/openclaw is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: openclaw/openclaw leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 29 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 29 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: openclaw/openclaw — 138 commits today and 2 same-day mapped articles, 417.5 below its current daily pace, with 163 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
NousResearch/hermes-agent — 32 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
yc-software/qm — No same-day commit after 123 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Find your Task-dependent plugins before upgrading OpenClaw
dailyInsight.insight: OpenClaw removed Tasks and TaskFlow from main while retaining background execution under Cron, session and native owners. The old public interfaces have no compatibility facade.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The SDK retirement removes Task APIs; Doctor imports eligible native recovery facts into existing session bindings only when requester ownership is established. Physical tables remain, so their presence cannot establish API compatibility.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: An operator can preserve stored records and still lose a plugin interface or encounter work whose completion cannot be safely reassigned.

actions.audience: OpenClaw operators evaluating a revision containing the Tasks removal
actions.label: Inventory Task integrations and rehearse unfinished work
actions.instruction: List plugins using runtime.tasks or the retired Task harness module. In a disposable copy with a matching backup, rehearse an upgrade with unfinished native work and inspect Doctor ownership warnings, result delivery and rollback before changing the live installation.
actions.effort: One plugin inventory and a disposable upgrade rehearsal

receipts.title: Remove Tasks and TaskFlow after ownership cutovers
receipts.supports: Removes public Task surfaces and records ownership-aware legacy assignment migration plus the bounded upgrade proof.

receipts.title: Removed SDK surfaces and retained storage
receipts.supports: Documents no compatibility facade, retained tables and the surviving runtime-specific operations.

confidence.basis: Landed code, migration definitions, regression cases and public SDK documentation agree on the interface removal and ownership boundary.

dailyInsight.limitation: We did not run an upgrade or verify installed release versions. The landing record leaves some native completion and 9.4 rollback witnesses unproven, and its earlier CI pass is not a fresh full pass on the final head.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise the audit if the targeted release restores compatibility or if a complete upgrade and rollback replay contradicts the documented migration boundary.
dailyInsight.watchNext: A completed published-package native completion and rollback replay, plus the first release contract that contains the removal.
